# Establishment log — popol-vuh-021 (image 0066 from line 13, 0067, 0068, 0069 lines 1–19)

Read 2026-11-28 by the routine's own model from source/pages/i0066 (from the indented `Are cut vae qui nabal qui camic`,
line 13, after `… xban chique.`), all of i0067 and i0068, and i0069 to `… ta xebec cut ruꜭ ahau.` (its nineteenth line),
in strips of about seven lines at 1.15–1.2×, with 1.6–2× crops of doubtful words, checked word by word against Brasseur
1861 (OCR lines c. 26494–26700, his chapter 12 `CABLAHPAH CHI TZIH`, and c. 26800–27000, the opening of his chapter 13).
Pillow in a scratch venv.

Start: `Are cut vae qui nabal` (0066 l.13). End: `… camol que ta xebec cut ruꜭ ahau.` (0069 l.19), a paragraph end in the
MS; the next line is the indented paragraph `Xe opon puch cuꜭ ahauab, que mocho chic …`, which begins popol-vuh-022.
Brasseur's chapter 13 runs on about two more pages (the dog, the burnt house, the sacrificed man, the death of Hun Came
and Vucub Came) to `… xa pu qui halvachibal quib ta xqui bano.`; 022 should end there. The part was ended at the
Ximénez paragraph break inside the images the packet gave (0066–0069), rather than carried two pages past them.
parts.json: 022 images set to 0069–0072 (was 0072–0074, which would have left 0069–0071 unread); plan.md row updated.

Content: chapter 12 — the twins, forewarned, instruct the seers Xulu and Pacam what to answer when Xibalba asks how to
dispose of their bones (not the ravine, not hung on trees; ground like maize and thrown into the river); the great
oven; the twins refuse the game of flying over it, embrace, and go face down into the fire together; Xibalba rejoices;
the bones ground and thrown into the river; they sink and become handsome boys. Chapter 13 (beginning) — on the fifth
day they appear as fish-men (vinac car), then as two ragged poor men dancing the Puhuy, Cux, Yboy, Xꜩul and Chiꜩic,
burning houses and restoring them, sacrificing each other and coming back to life; the lords hear and send for them;
the twins protest that they are ashamed to go before the lords; they are driven along by the messengers.

Paragraphs: Ximénez's indents at `Are cut vae` (0066), `Chi robix cut` (0068) and `Cate chi puch roponic` (0068); the
others (`Ta xe pixabah`, `Are ca ban ri nima chohim abah`, `Que quicot`, `Catecut qui taquic`, `Xe opon cut cuꜭ ri
xahol`, `Xelehebex`) are ours at the sense joints, as 015–020.

## Folios
0066 carries `28` at the top left (28v), 0068 `29` (29v); so 0067 = 29r, 0069 = 30r → `fols. 28v–30r`.

## Nested speech
The twins' instructions to Xulu and Pacam quote what Xibalba will ask and what the seers are to answer
(`Vve que ꜭha chive: …, quix ꜭha.`), and the messenger's summons quotes the lord (`ca quix ca chohih, caꜭha ahau`,
`quecha ahauab, quix ꜭha chique`); printed inside one pair of “ ” with colons and the K'iche' speech verbs marking the
inner speech, as 017 (the pin check counts ‘ ’ as apostrophes).

## Letters decided by the hand against Brasseur, or doubtful
- 0066 l.20 `honel chicop` — the MS has a clear looped h; Brasseur's OCR `попе!` (nonel?). Printed `honel`; doubtful word.
- 0066 l.21 `chicop` followed by an ink blot (a struck o?); read `chicop ꜭo` with Brasseur `chicop qo`.
- 0066 l.22–23 `nicvachinel` (MS `nicvachi-nel`), one word; Brasseur's OCR is garbled here. Doubtful division.
- 0066 l.27 `ca qui nuc`: MS `caquinuc`, Brasseur `ca qui nuk` (his k = plain q, so c).
- 0066 l.28 `mixoh` — the h overwritten/blotted; read with Brasseur `mi-x-oh`.
- 0066 l.30 `choc` (MS `ch-oc` across the line); Brasseur `ch'oc`.
- 0066 l.32 `ca ꜭux` — MS letter q-shaped; Brasseur `ka qux`; ꜭ.
- 0066 l.35 `ta coh camic`: MS `tacoh`, Brasseur `ta koh`.
- 0066 l.36 `Vue` — written so here (elsewhere `vve`); kept as written.
- 0066 l.38 `ta coh catoc`: MS clearly c; Brasseur `gat-oc` (his g = ꜫ). MS followed; the drafter should note Brasseur.
- 0066 l.39 `xchi cu chah`: MS `xchi|cuchah`, a vertical stroke between (a later divider?); read with Brasseur `x-ch'y cu chah`.
- 0066 l.40 `Ma vꜩ lo` — Brasseur omits these words; the MS has them.
- 0066 l.43 `chi ꜭaztah` — MS g-shaped letter (cuatrillo), Brasseur `qaztah`; but 0068 l.27 `chi caztah` and 0069 `ca qui
  caztah` have plain c, as the published parts' `caztah`. Both kept as written.
- 0067 l.10 `cahim hal`: MS c; Brasseur `qahim` (ꜭ). MS followed.
- 0067 l.11 `cu chi queic`: MS `cuchiqueic`.
- 0067 l.14 `cutunizah`, 0068 `cutun` (three times): MS c; Brasseur `qutun-` (ꜭ). MS followed, as the published `cutun`.
- 0067 l.21–22 `achbilai que`: Brasseur `achbilay que`; division as his.
- 0067 l.29 `ca quiy`: the MS has `ca qui` with a raised hooked mark after it; read as y with Brasseur `ka quiy`. Doubtful.
- 0067 l.33 `quetaam` (MS `queta-am`); Brasseur `k'etaam`.
- 0067 l.35 `chi vi tana` (MS `chivi / tana`); Brasseur `chi vi tana`.
- 0067 l.44 `qui taquic` — the t written like f; Brasseur `qui takic`.
- 0068 l.1 `xe ꜫihin`: MS g-shaped letter; Brasseur `x-e gihin` (g = ꜫ); ꜫ printed (q'ij 'day, divine'). Doubtful letter.
- 0068 l.13–14 `aꜩiyac … aꜩiiac … aꜩiiac` — the second and third are written with ii (no y descender); kept as written.
  A `?` stands in the right margin of this line (later hand?); ignored.
- 0068 l.14 `pu quih`, `cul qui cu`: Brasseur `gili`(?), `qul qui qu`; MS followed (plain c, quih).
- 0068 l.19 `Chiꜩic` — the letter after `chi` has the ꜩ shape (as in `Xꜩul` on the same line) with a mark over it;
  Brasseur `Chitic`. Printed Chiꜩic; doubtful, the drafter should give Brasseur's reading.
- 0068 l.21–23 `libah chi cut chi vinaquir chic` (Brasseur's OCR garbled here).
- 0068 l.30 `v xenacahic`: Brasseur's OCR `u xeaaahic`; MS clear. Meaning uncertain.
- 0068 l.36, 40 `cuz` — the MS letter is q-shaped (`quz`) both times; Brasseur `cuz`. Printed cuz; doubtful letter (ꜭ?).
- 0068 l.45 `xꜭhao`: MS `xqhao`; Brasseur `x-chao`.
- 0069 l.1 `chi cah`: Brasseur's OCR `chi аһ`.
- 0069 l.4 `qui iꜩel`: MS `quiiꜩel`; Brasseur `qui itzel`.
- 0069 l.8 `ꜭo cam cu raih nay pu ri`: MS `gocam curaih nay pu ri`; Brasseur `qo qam cu raih naipu`. ꜭo with Brasseur;
  `cam` plain as the MS; `nay pu` divided (MS `naypu`).
- 0069 l.12 `ca cah vi`: MS c; Brasseur `ca k'ah vi`.
- 0069 l.15 `chuvi cax, cacrail`: MS plain c; Brasseur `chuvi qax cakrail`.
- 0069 l.17 `xa chi mach cay`: Brasseur `xa chi macheay`.
